title: A Girl With Months To Live Was Killed By A Stranger Before She Could Say Goodbye . . .
caption:
Sakura Yamauchi is dying of a pancreatic disease in I Want to Eat Your Pancreas, and only one quiet classmate knows. 😭 A boy who never cared about anyone is pulled into her last summer.

#iwanttoeatyourpancreas #anime #animemovie #animerecap #fyp
comment: Would you have told Kyoko the truth, or kept Sakura's secret like he did? Why?
credit: Anime: I Want to Eat Your Pancreas (2018)

segments.say: A girl who knew she was dying got stabbed by a stranger, and the boy heard about it on the *news*.
To see how it got here, go back to a hospital *lobby*.
A quiet boy finds a *diary* that someone left on a bench, and he starts to read.
It is called Living with Dying, and the writer has a deadly pancreatic *disease*.
Then its owner walks up and takes it back. She is Sakura, the most popular girl in his *class*.
She says she is really dying. He shrugs and says, that is too *bad*.
Sakura bursts out laughing. Nobody has ever reacted so *calmly*.
She makes him promise to keep her illness a *secret*.
He has no friends to tell anyway, which is exactly why she picked *him*.
The next week, she turns up as his partner at the school *library*.
She shows him her bucket list, and he is now her official *helper*.
Her first wish is barbecue, and she orders a plate of organ meat, even the *pancreas*.
She says some people believe that if someone eats you, your soul lives on *inside* them.
Weirdest friendship ever.
He admits his hobby is imagining what everyone thinks of him. He never *asks*.
On the walk home, two thugs shove an old woman to the *ground*.
Sakura does not think twice. She steps in front of them and *shouts*.
The thugs run, and the boy asks why she took such a *risk*.
She says taking risks is easy when you know you are going to *die*.
At a cafe called Spring, she says cherry blossoms always wait for the right time to *bloom*.
She makes him swap numbers and texts him, be my friend until I *die*.
At school, the whole class starts whispering about the two of *them*.
Sakura drags him to a buffet. Then her best friend Kyoko walks in and *explodes*.
He finally asks, are you really going to die? She says yes, but with him she feels *normal*.
Then she drags him on a surprise overnight trip, telling her parents she is with *Kyoko*.
They eat ramen, laugh in the street, and she writes all of it in her *diary*.
At the hotel, a booking mix-up gives them one *room*.
That night she pulls out a deck of cards and makes him play truth or *dare*.
She asks who the prettiest girl in class is. When it is his turn, he ranks her *third*.
After a few drinks she cannot stand, so he has to carry her to *bed*.
Late that night she asks what he would do if she admitted she was terrified of *dying*.
Back home, Kyoko corners him. If he ever hurts Sakura, she will make him *regret* it.
A week later, Sakura invites him over to borrow her favorite book, The Little *Prince*.
Then she pulls a cruel prank on him, and he *freezes*.
On the road home, a boy steps out of the rain with an umbrella. It is Takahiro, Sakura's *ex*.
He asks why she wastes her time on someone so *depressing*.
Then he throws a punch, right as Sakura turns the *corner*.
What a coward move.
Sakura screams at him never to come near them *again*.
In the rain, the boy says people like him should stay away. Sakura says every small choice led them *here*.

segments.text: I'm really happy that you're here with me right now.

segments.say: She begs him to stay by her side a little *longer*.
After that, he follows her bucket list: bowling, photo booths, and *karaoke*.
But halfway through the list, she collapses, and he finds her room in the *hospital*.
She hides her fear behind a smile and a card game. She asks him what being alive *means*.
He thinks hard and says it means reaching the hearts of the *people* around you.
Sakura hugs him and says she loves feeling someone's *warmth*.
Kyoko walks in and finds them hugging, but Sakura still keeps her *secret*.
That night she sneaks him out to a dark hill to watch the city *lights*.
There he says what he cannot hide anymore. He wants her to *live*.

segments.text: I promise. When I'm going to die, I'll be sure to let you know.

segments.say: Then the sky explodes in *fireworks*.
Back home, his mom is happy he finally has someone who sees him for *himself*.
On his way to meet her, he takes gum from his old classmate for the first *time*.
At the cafe, he finally types the message she has been waiting to *hear*.
He sends it. But Sakura never *answers*.
Later that night, a news reporter reads out a name he *knows*.
Sakura was stabbed on the street by a stranger, and she did not *survive*.
She broke her promise to warn him. And he never gave back her *book*.
He skips the funeral and hides at home for ten days, too *scared* to face it.
When he finally walks to her house, her mother is waiting. He tells her he knew about the *illness*.
Then he asks for her diary, and her mother says Sakura meant for him to *have* it.
He opens it, and the first page is the day they met, the 22nd of *April*.
She wrote that he was strange and quiet, and she liked him *immediately*.
She wrote about the barbecue, and the nights she cried alone after he *left*.
And she wrote that his visit made her the happiest she had ever *been*.
Near the end, one page is meant just for *him*.
She wrote that it was not love and not friendship, but something *else*.
She knew why he never said her name. He was afraid of losing *her*.
She said she always looked up to him, because even a coward has *charm*.
She waited for him to need her, just like cherry blossoms wait for *spring*.

segments.text: I want to eat your pancreas.

segments.say: Her last line is the same one he sent her. I want to eat your *pancreas*.
Her mother hands him Sakura's phone. His last message was *read*.
Then he cries harder than he ever has in his *life*.
Her mother asks his name, and for the first time he says it. Haruki, spring tree. Sakura, cherry *blossom*.
Weeks later, he asks Kyoko to meet him at Sakura's favorite *cafe*.
He slides the diary across the table and tells her Sakura was *dying*.
Kyoko reads it, shaking. Why did nobody tell her *sooner*?
She says it is his fault, and she will never *forgive* him.
He bows and says, maybe someday, we could be *friends*.
A year later, he stands at Sakura's grave beside *Kyoko*.
Sakura is gone, but the boy she changed is finally learning how to *live*.
